reading: Every solid square shrinks by one cell on each side (9x9->7x7, 5x5->3x3, 3x3->single cell), while a single cell grows into a 9x9 square centred on it; same colours, background 7.
verb: shrink squares one ring / grow dots to 9x9

slots.subject: each solid single-colour square object
slots.size_rule: side n -> n-2 for n>1; side 1 -> 9 (centred on the dot)
slots.anchor: object's own box, inset by one on top-left

why: each output object is the input object's box inset by one, except 1x1 objects which become 9x9 centred

reading: Every object loses its two leftmost columns (relative to its own bounding box); objects only two columns wide vanish.

slots.subject: each single-colour object
slots.cut: cells in the first two columns of the object's bbox become background

why: output object = input object minus its two leftmost bbox columns
invariants: all other cells of each object

reading: Two shapes overlap; the shape that was underneath is brought to the front, so the overlap cells take the hidden shape's colour.

slots.subject: overlap cells: cells of the top shape that lie on the hidden shape's (completed) extent

why: only cells where the occluded shape would continue change, and they become that shape's colour

reading: Each yellow rectangle containing k dots of colour c gets a solid surrounding border of colour c, k cells thick.

slots.subject: each colour-4 rectangle
slots.colour: colour of the dots inside it

why: ring around each rectangle's box has thickness = dot count and dot colour

reading: Plus shapes whose centres lie on a common diagonal are joined by a diagonal line of colour 2 through the background cells between them.

new_rows.name: diag_link
new_rows.datalog:
fg(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
ctr(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), Y1 = Y - 1, cell(Y1, X, C), Y2 = Y + 1, cell(Y2, X, C), X1 = X - 1, cell(Y, X1, C), X2 = X + 1, cell(Y, X2, C).
diag_link(YC, XC) :- ctr(Y, X), ctr(Y2, X2), D = Y2 - Y, D > 0, E = X2 - X, E = D, px(YC, XC, C), YC > Y, YC < Y2, K = YC - Y, XC = X + K, !fg(YC, XC).
diag_link(YC, XC) :- ctr(Y, X), ctr(Y2, X2), D = Y2 - Y, D > 0, E = X - X2, E = D, px(YC, XC, C), YC > Y, YC < Y2, K = YC - Y, XC = X - K, !fg(YC, XC).

why: every new 2 cell lies strictly between two diagonally aligned plus centres; nothing else changes

reading: Each object (resting on the bottom) is lifted straight up by a distance equal to its own height.
why: each output object = input object shifted up by its bbox height, shape kept

reading: The whole grid is filled with the most frequent colour of the input.

slots.colour: most common colour of the input

why: output is uniform in the input's majority colour

reading: Colour-9 pieces stay fixed; every other piece attached to a 9 slides straight away from that 9 until it reaches the grid border, keeping its shape.

new_rows.name: sat
new_rows.datalog: sat(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), C < 9.

why: each non-9 piece keeps its shape and ends touching the border on the side facing away from its 9 neighbour

reading: The green shape slides toward the red bar until it touches it, and a full bar of 8 is drawn right behind the shape on the side away from the red bar.
verb: slide to bar and back with 8 bar

slots.subject: the colour-3 object
slots.added: full line of 8 adjacent to the moved shape on the far side

why: shape keeps its form and touches the 2 line; one 8 line parallel to it touches the shape's opposite side

reading: A 2x2 colour key sits in a corner; each dot in the main area is recoloured with the key colour of the quadrant of the area it lies in.

slots.key: the 2x2 colour block in the 8-bordered corner
slots.subject: dots in the main (non-8) area
slots.map: key scaled up to the area: quadrant (top/bottom, left/right) -> key cell colour

why: each dot cell takes the colour of the key cell for its quadrant; nothing else changes
